- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) and forecast is below recent low, model tends to underreact — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is above recent high, model tends to overreact — adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.0+), especially in early 30d horizon — reduce forecast by 5–10% of peak value.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- In 30d horizon, model consistently underestimates downward moves after negative sentiment clusters — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to downward forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag — delay correction by 1–2 days and apply smoother decay curve.
